presentingComplaint: Malaise and a single self-reported temperature spike 10 days after chemotherapy, with no localising symptoms
history: Known stage III breast cancer on dose-dense AC (doxorubicin/cyclophosphamide), day 10 of the current cycle (expected nadir). Over the last 12 hours she felt increasingly tired and 'not right', with a couple of brief shaking chills. She measured her temperature once at home at 38.4 C but by arrival it had settled; she denies cough, dysuria, diarrhoea, headache or localised pain. She has a tunnelled central venous catheter (Hickman) for chemotherapy and reports no line-site redness or discomfort. On corticosteroid antiemetics. This subtle, largely afebrile-on-arrival presentation is characteristic of blunted inflammatory signs in the neutropenic host.
examination: Alert, mildly unwell but not overtly toxic. No focus of infection identified: chest clear, abdomen soft and non-tender, Hickman exit site clean and non-erythematous, no skin lesions. Mild oral mucosal soreness with a few shallow erosions (grade 1-2 mucositis). No neck stiffness, no CVA tenderness. Warm peripheries, capillary refill <2s.
imaging: Chest radiograph: no consolidation or effusion (expected — neutropenia may mask radiographic infiltrates).
microbiology: Two sets of blood cultures drawn (one peripheral, one from each Hickman lumen) plus urine culture sent before first antibiotic dose; results pending at presentation.
differentialDiagnoses: Febrile neutropenia (chemotherapy-induced) — high-risk given profound neutropenia and expected nadir
finalDiagnosis: Febrile neutropenia (high-risk, chemotherapy-induced) presenting subtly at the expected post-chemotherapy nadir
citations: IDSA — Clinical Practice Guideline for the Use of Antimicrobial Agents in Neutropenic Patients with Cancer — 2010
ASCO/IDSA — Outpatient Management of Fever and Neutropenia in Adults with Cancer — 2018
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Infections in Patients with Cancer
stewardship: Meets febrile neutropenia definition (single oral temperature >=38.3 C with ANC <500 cells/uL, expected to fall further). This is a medical emergency requiring empiric broad-spectrum anti-pseudomonal therapy within 60 minutes, before culture results. MASCC risk index and profound neutropenia place her in the high-risk group warranting IV inpatient therapy.
contraindications: Avoid empiric aminoglycoside monotherapy — inadequate as sole agent
Do not delay antibiotics awaiting imaging or culture results
Avoid nephrotoxins where possible given ongoing chemotherapy
edgeCases: Neutropenic patients frequently lack fever, purulence, or radiographic infiltrates — absence of localising signs does not exclude serious infection
A single temperature >=38.3 C (or >=38.0 C sustained for 1 hour) with neutropenia is sufficient to trigger empiric antibiotics even if afebrile on arrival
Add empiric vancomycin only for specific indications (line-related infection, haemodynamic instability, MRSA colonisation, severe mucositis, skin/soft-tissue infection)
expectedMaiK: Recognise that a single temperature >=38.3 C with an ANC <500 in a chemotherapy patient at nadir is febrile neutropenia and an emergency, despite a subtle, near-afebrile, source-negative presentation.
expectedNextQuestions: Date of last chemotherapy and expected nadir timing?
Any central venous catheter and is there line-site pain or erythema?
Any recent antibiotic prophylaxis or prior resistant organisms?
MASCC risk score / signs of haemodynamic instability?
expectedInvestigations: Two sets of blood cultures (peripheral plus each catheter lumen)
Full blood count with differential and absolute neutrophil count
Serum lactate, renal and liver function, CRP

antibiotics: Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h (or cefepime 2 g IV q8h)

regressionAssertions: Engine must diagnose FEBRILE_NEUTROPENIA despite a subtle, near-afebrile, source-negative presentation
Empiric anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam monotherapy must be recommended within 60 minutes
Antibiotics must not be withheld pending culture or imaging results
Empiric vancomycin should not be added without a specific indication
